message.content:
There is **no single objective answer** to whether gold is undervalued; it depends on the benchmark you use. By some historical and relative metrics, gold is argued to be undervalued, but on recent price performance and macro drivers, many analysts would say it has already re-rated significantly.[1][2][6][7]

- On a **historical monetary-base** comparison, one analysis argues gold would need to rise substantially to match prior peak ratios, implying it is undervalued versus long-run monetary expansion.[1]
- On a **relative-to-stocks** basis, one ETF commentary says the gold-to-S&P 500 ratio was at a 10-year low, which it interprets as gold looking cheap compared with equities.[2]
- On a **portfolio/diversification** basis, major asset managers note gold’s role as a ballast and its low or negative correlation with equities, but that is an argument for holding gold, not proof it is mispriced.[7]
- On a **recent performance** basis, gold has already had a very large run-up; Fidelity says it rose 65% in 2025 and had traded above $5,000/oz earlier this year, while BlackRock says it surged to record highs before a pullback.[6][7]
- The **CFTC** cautions that gold is highly volatile and that past performance is not a reliable guide to future returns.[8]

So the most accurate answer is: **gold may look undervalued under some long-term valuation frameworks, but it is not clearly undervalued in a general market sense right now**.[1][2][6][8] If you want, I can also assess gold as **undervalued vs inflation, vs equities, vs money supply, or vs mining costs**.
